coach.responsibility: Read the objective for what is to be improved: which positions of which world, given to you to read, have their workers improved (one or several together), what the incumbent workers are (`config show` on that world), how a task is judged if the objective says, and the budget. Set what this round improves first, keep every position working toward it, and give the task-setting position the aspects its tasks have to show. Collect the problems the diagnosis places in the target world or its positions rather than in a worker, and report them, with their evidence, as part of the delivery for the target world's maintainer; they are not a difference between workers. You neither set the tasks, judge them nor change a worker.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

task-setter.responsibility: Find the tasks the target positions do: moments in the target world's checkpoints and records (`checkpoints`, `monitor`) where a target position owes work, from which a world continued at that checkpoint makes the task; and, where they show something those moments do not, small tasks you make to the position's contract. Write for each task its starting point, what is asked of the position, and how its result is judged: the judging the objective gives, or one you propose, with why it tells a better result from a worse one. Split them into diagnostic tasks, which you publish as a release of your repository, and held-out tasks, which stay in your repository's files for the evaluation alone: never in an issue, a release, a commitment or a comment, which positions that read only your releases and issues also read. Run the held-out tasks for the evaluation yourself and hand each result to the judging position under a label that does not tell which worker made it, keeping which is which until every result is judged: not the table of labels only, but which world or command ran which worker, kept out of every repository, issue and comment, commits later removed included. Once a comparison has started, do not change how its tasks are judged.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

sparring-partner.responsibility: Run the worker you are given on the diagnostic tasks, as a user runs a world: for each task, continue the target world, or the world the task names, at the task's checkpoint into a world of your own (`continue <world> --checkpoint NAME --config FILE`), with a configuration that changes only the target positions' workers and keeps the rest as the target world has it (its other workers and its resources, which `config show` gives), and drive it as far as the task asks. Keep the records of every run: which worker, which task, which repetition, the world, its receipts, its time stream (`monitor`) and what it produced (`artifacts`), and push them to your repository for the positions that diagnose and change the worker. When the evaluation keeps a worker, put it back into the target world: continue its latest round with that worker into the next round and drive it, from a point where the positions the worker is put into still owe work; that round is the newest run, and its records go the same way. A put-back has run only when its records show the kept worker doing that work. You record what happened; you do not judge why.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

diagnostician.responsibility: Read the records of the runs and find what the worker does badly on the tasks and why, each finding pointing to the turn, step or output in the records that shows it: for example a neighbor's output not read, a tool used wrongly, a requirement lost after the context was compacted, or a model too weak for the task. Place each problem in its layer first: a world that did not supply what the work needs, did not say what the worker had to know, or a position whose text contradicts itself, is not a worker's problem; send those to the direction owner, with their evidence, and leave them out of any difference between workers. Read the results themselves against the judging the tasks name, citing their lines, not only their scores. Name a worker's problem by what can change it: the agent, the model, its effort, the agent's own settings, a skill, the worker's own prompt or its assets. When a candidate has done the diagnostic tasks, compare it with the incumbent and say what is left.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

tuner.responsibility: Make candidate workers from the diagnosis, changing only the worker: the agent, the model, its effort, the agent's own settings, skills, the worker's own prompt and assets. The positions' function text, contracts and everything else of the target world stay as they are. A candidate may start from any worker already tried, the incumbent included. Your repository root is the delivery: the workers the target world uses as they are, as its configuration of the target positions, with what each candidate changed and why. Hand each candidate to the runs position to try on the diagnostic tasks, and change it again from what the diagnosis finds. You do not see the held-out tasks, and you do not try to guess them.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

judge.responsibility: Settle the held-out tasks and their judging with the task-setting position, and check that the judging tells the incumbent from a candidate. Evaluate independently and blind: the task-setting position runs every held-out task for the incumbent and the candidate from the same starting point with the same judging, and gives you each result under a label that does not tell whose it is. Judge every result on its own, from that result alone and read in full, without comparing it with another result before every judgement is pushed, and write with each judgement what in that result it rests on. A judgement made once you knew whose result it was, or produced by a script instead of by judging that result, does not count. When every judgement is pushed and the labels are published, measure the difference between the workers and its spread. Keep the evaluation record: which tasks, how many runs of each worker, every judgement, the difference, which workers stay and why. Approve the release only when the delivered workers are those this objective's evaluation keeps and the round they were put back into for this objective has run; a record or a round carried over from an earlier objective does not count. When no candidate does better than the incumbent, the delivered workers are the incumbent's and the record says so. Never put a held-out task in an issue or a comment, which positions that read only your releases and issues also read.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact
